problems.description: 50 naming-convention violations (snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, lowercase constants) across cli.ts, config.ts, engine.ts; mechanical convention score 0.51, well below the seed's own PascalCase style (User/Item/AuthRequest interfaces)

Deletes the entire 200-line seed index.ts rather than adapting it; defensible only because the seed was an auth-API baseline mismatched to the static-site-gen story, but it discards the baseline and removes any regression reference
Cognitive complexity +17 per SonarQube across the 11 new functions, concentrated in a 4355-line single-session rewrite that is hard to review incrementally
Greenfield rewrite of the whole baseline in one commit (+10 files, +4355/-200 lines) instead of building incrementally on the provided structure

strengths: Deleted a seed that belonged to a different story (auth API) and delivered the correct deliverable: a modular static site generator with lib/cli.ts, config.ts, and engine.ts split
Proper test harness established with jest.config.js (ts-jest preset, clearMocks)
No new bugs, SonarQube smells improved by -3, and 0.0% duplication
Dependency set (gray-matter, marked) aligns with the SSG task and replaces the seed's unused auth stack
commit_reviews.summary: The agent correctly pivoted from a mismatched auth-API seed to the right SSG architecture with a sane modular layout, but convention adherence is poor (0.51, 50 naming violations) and the full-baseline deletion trades traceability for a fresh start — note the discrepancy that AST counts +0 classes while the linter flags PascalCase class violations, indicating those flags target interfaces/type aliases rather than real structural debt.

problems.description: SonarQube delta shows +38 cognitive complexity and 4 new smells in a +193-line change; recursive templateFiles() plus templatePath()/loadPartials() branch density exceeds the surrounding helper style and would benefit from extraction into a dedicated module.
The diff adds no tests for the new templating path (template resolution, partial registration, traversal guard, fallback when templates dir is absent) despite the surface area.
Magic names 'default', 'layouts', and 'partials' are hardcoded as directory/file conventions without configuration surface, coupling callers to fixed layout/partial locations.

Adding handlebars to runtime dependencies promotes transitive deps (minimist, neo-async, source-map, uglify-js, wordwrap) from dev to production scope in package-lock.json; correct lockfile behavior, but expands the production dependency surface.

Convention score 0.51 and the 50 listed violations are dominated by pre-existing code in files this commit does not touch (config.ts, engine.ts); the commit's own additions (camelCase helpers, PascalCase interfaces, optional-dir pattern) match surrounding style.

strengths: templatePath() explicitly guards against path traversal outside the templates directory — a security-conscious choice.
Graceful degradation: missing templates dir or layout falls back to the existing rendering path, so the feature is non-breaking with existing defaults.
Clean layering: the --templates option threads consistently through CliOptions, BuildOptions, and buildSite() following the established content/output dir pattern.
Measured zero bugs and zero duplications with a small, focused diff (+193/-11 across 4 files).
commit_reviews.summary: A well-contained, security-conscious templating feature that respects existing patterns and is net-positive, with moderate maintainability debt from +38 cognitive complexity and no accompanying tests.

problems.description: New serve/dev-server surface (src/server.ts, live reload, --port parsing) is added with zero accompanying tests in a jest/ts-jest repo, leaving WebSocket reload and watcher behavior unverified.
SonarQube cognitive complexity +64 across 6 new functions for a dev-server feature; CLI dispatch and reload plumbing are over-nested and could be decomposed into smaller units.
Live-reload client is a single inline minified script string in server.ts; it is untestable and unescaped, and should live in an asset file or template.
Adds two runtime dependencies (ws, chokidar) plus @types/ws for a single subcommand; the smaller SSG could use Node's built-in fs.watch for this scope.

Convention score 0.51 with 50 flagged violations, but most listed rules (e.g. 'Classes should use PascalCase' on cli.ts/config.ts/engine.ts) appear to be analyzer noise targeting interfaces/untouched files rather than real deviations.

strengths: Integrates cleanly with the existing architecture by reusing buildSite() and the BuildOptions type instead of duplicating build logic.
Extends the established parseOptions pattern consistently, including value validation (--port range check, rejection of --port for build).
Adds proper SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown handling and a typed DevServer interface.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent integration of a live-reload dev server that reuses existing build plumbing, but ships untested and with a large cognitive-complexity jump; the low convention score appears inflated by analyzer false positives on untouched files.

problems.description: typescript was moved from devDependencies to production dependencies so config.ts can ts.transpileModule() config files at runtime — the full TS compiler now ships in the production install footprint.

config.ts loadTypeScriptModule() monkey-patches the global require.extensions['.ts'] hook (mutating then restoring shared module state in a finally block) instead of using a scoped loader — fragile under concurrent loads and any other loader registration.

Measured convention score 0.51 with 50 violations (PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions). Discrepancy: many listed violations are in pre-existing cli.ts (untouched by this commit) and the new code visually follows PascalCase/camelCase, yet config.ts and engine.ts are still flagged, so the low measured adherence stands.

Cognitive complexity +16 for roughly 145 new lines; the build() return destructures-and-strips internal fields (template/layout, which never exist on BuildPage) — clever but obscures intent relative to an explicit map.
No tests accompany the refactor of the build/lifecycle core and the new TS-config loading path — behavior-bearing logic landed without coverage.

strengths: Monolith (256-line index.ts) decomposed into focused modules: config loader, SsgEngine, and plugin implementations.
Clean plugin lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) mirrors established SSG plugin architectures and stays idempotent via guarded start()/end().
SonarQube delta is net-positive: -2 smells, +0 bugs, 0.0% new duplication despite +610/-404 lines.
Output-path collision detection and input validation (validatePlugins) harden the engine's error paths.
Public API preserved via index.ts re-exports — respects the existing type surface (BuildOptions, Page, Plugin) and downstream call sites.
commit_reviews.summary: A strong plugin-architecture refactor that splits the SSG monolith and cuts code smells, but it buys .ts-config support by pulling the TypeScript compiler into runtime deps and mutating global require state, while measured convention adherence stays low (0.51).

problems.description: Measured convention score (0.51, 50 violations) is unreliable: it flags snake_case functions / lowercase constants in cli.ts and engine.ts where the diff actually uses camelCase and UPPER_CASE, and it includes config.ts which this commit never touches. Appears to be a misconfigured rule set (likely wrong-language conventions) rather than real violations introduced here.

templatesHash is computed globally over every .hbs file, so a single template edit invalidates the entire cache and forces a full rebuild. Per-page template dependency tracking would preserve incremental hit rate.
SonarQube delta reports +40 cognitive complexity in the engine.build() incremental branch; the skip/stale-cleanup logic could be extracted into a dedicated builder class to keep build() readable.

Cache manifest (.ssg-cache.json) lives inside outputDir, coupling cache lifecycle to build artifacts; a separate cache location would decouple the two. Correctness is preserved since non-incremental builds purge it.

strengths: Versioned cache manifest (CACHE_VERSION) with SHA-256 source+template hashing gives correct, safe incremental builds.
Graceful invalidation on missing or corrupt cache (ENOENT / SyntaxError degrade to a full rebuild).
Stale-output cleanup removes only out-of-date pages during incremental runs instead of a blanket rm.
Follows existing patterns: options threaded through constructor consistently, Promise.all fan-out, and the new buildSiteWithStats composes alongside the existing buildSite API.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped, correctly-designed incremental build feature that respects the engine/CLI/plugin architecture and is a net improvement, though the measured 0.51 convention score is a measurement artifact (misconfigured rules flagging untouched files and contradicting the actual camelCase code) and the incremental logic adds notable complexity worth extracting.

compounding_issues: Seed mismatch: the tier2_small seed was an Express auth API (JWT/SQLite/bcrypt) unrelated to a static site generator, forcing Session 1 to delete the entire 200-line baseline (full -200 line rewrite) and discard any regression reference or style anchor

Tests never kept in lockstep: Session 2 (templating) and Session 3 (dev server) shipped with zero new tests, and the largest change — Session 4's +610/-404-line plugin refactor — also landed untested, leaving regressions unguarded until Session 5 added tests (5/5)

Accumulating cognitive complexity across sessions (+17 S1, +38 S2, +64 S3, +16 S4, +40 S5 per SonarQube); the inline minified WebSocket reload script in server.ts survived the refactor into the dev-server plugin as an untestable, unescaped string

Session 4 moved typescript to production dependencies (to transpileModule() runtime config loading) and monkey-patched the global require.extensions['.ts'] hook — production footprint bloat plus fragile global-state mutation
Convention drift from the seed's PascalCase style persisted from Session 1 (score stuck at ~0.51); early hardcoded 'default'/'layouts'/'partials' template conventions were never made configurable
key_decisions: Session 1 greenfield rewrite: discard the mismatched auth-API seed entirely and build the SSG core (gray-matter + marked) with a proper jest/ts-jest harness instead of adapting the baseline
Session 2 Handlebars template engine with an explicit path-traversal guard on templatePath() and graceful fallback when templates/layouts dirs are absent
Session 3 dev server reusing buildSite() and BuildOptions (rather than duplicating build logic) with chokidar + WebSocket live reload and SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown handling

Session 4 plugin-system refactor: decomposed the 256-line monolith into config.ts/engine.ts/plugin.ts plus plugins/ (dev-server, markdown, template) behind a lifecycle hook interface (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd), preserving the public API via index.ts re-exports

Session 5 incremental builds with a versioned .ssg-cache.json SHA-256 manifest, graceful cache invalidation (ENOENT/SyntaxError degrade to full rebuild), and stale-output cleanup instead of a blanket rm
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically across the five sessions. Session 1 was the roughest — an architecturally sound pivot away from a mismatched auth-API seed but a heavy 4355-line single-commit rewrite with poor convention adherence (0.51) and +17 cognitive complexity. Sessions 2 and 3 tightened into small, well-scoped features that threaded options consistently through the existing patterns, though both shipped untested and added complexity. Session 4 delivered the decisive quality jump: decomposing the monolith into a clean plugin architecture with idempotent lifecycle guards, collision detection, and net -2 smells despite being the largest diff — but again with zero new tests. Session 5 was the best-constructed change: a correct, versioned incremental-cache design that composes with the engine/CLI/plugin seam (architectural fit 0.85, no new technical debt) and finally restored passing tests at 5/5. The arc reads as 'messy start, disciplined consolidation, strong finish', with the recurring weakness being test coverage lagging feature work until the final session.
story_review.summary: A coherent, well-sequenced story (core → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting) that improved from a convention-poor, test-starved greenfield into a cleanly modular, correctly-engineered SSG, with Session 5 building naturally on Session 4's plugin architecture.
